replies.author: @josephcinquemani
replies.text:
5 million of that 8 million are Brooklyn & Queens. They’re on the Island but aren’t included when discussing LI as a political or cultural identity - though strong bonds were there a century ago and culturally, much of LI’s population is 1-3 generations removed from living in the City.

Queens and Brooklyn are pretty well served by the three bridges to the Bronx, and of Nassau’s 1.4 million residents, half are arguably better served by the Throg’s Neck & Whitestone than an Oyster Bay or King’s Park/Smithtown crossing. A bridge would be a time-saver for that portion of the remaining 2 million residents who wanted to go north for vacations, day-trips or business, but realistically, increased subsidized ferry service (keeping the cost under $40-$50) would suffice car traffic, and a couple rail terminals with increased freight rail (along the LIE) would reduce the trucks and be the better option for longterm growth and short-term relief. Probably better bang for our buck. Route the ferries to multiple CT and RI connections to induce local economic activity on the New England end.  A city and island with this much activity should make better use of the waterways, as we once did.
